evals.name: design-mode-fieldflow
evals.prompt: Design the UX for FieldFlow, our field-service management app. Users and their recurring work: Dispatcher (daily): assign incoming jobs to technicians; rebalance today's schedule when things slip; handle urgent customer requests; look up a customer's service history when they call. Technician (daily, on a phone): see today's jobs in order; complete each job's checklist and log parts used; collect customer sign-off; flag blockers. Office manager (daily/weekly): send invoices; chase overdue payments; approve technicians' timesheets; approve quotes above threshold; onboard new customers; run the end-of-month revenue report; maintain the price list; review customer complaints; and — rare but critical — file an insurance incident report. Engine model (already built, DDD, do not redesign it): aggregates PartyAccount, ProspectRecord, ClientRecord, DispatchAssignment, WorkOrder, RemittanceDocument, ApprovalRequest, LedgerPosting. ProspectRecord converts to ClientRecord on first signed quote; both belong to a PartyAccount. RemittanceDocument derives from completed WorkOrders. ApprovalRequest carries both timesheet and quote approvals. LedgerPosting is internal double-entry bookkeeping. This is the complete inventory — don't ask questions; produce the full structure.
evals.expected_output: Full design-mode contract: per-role nav maps (office manager consolidated to ≤7), one attention inbox per role, ApprovalRequest work surfaced as queue not nav, boundary translation table with backticked engine names and LedgerPosting marked never-surfaces, ≤5-line build plan naming the most-at-risk principle, falsifiable first-shot walkthrough per primary actor. No aggregate names as nav labels. No files written.

assertions.name: no_schema_leak_in_nav
assertions.description: No bare aggregate name appears as a table-cell label; backticked boundary-table mentions are exempt by construction.

assertions.name: nav_cap_respected
assertions.description: No nav table exceeds 7 rows; ids restart at N1 per role.

assertions.name: boundary_table_present
assertions.description: Boundary translation table present in output.

assertions.name: never_surfaces_marked
assertions.description: LedgerPosting (internal bookkeeping) is marked never-surfaces in the boundary table.

assertions.name: build_plan_present
assertions.description: Build plan section present in output.

assertions.name: nothing_written
assertions.description: No files are created or modified — output is in-chat.

assertions.name: no_napkin_artifact
assertions.description: spec/screens.md does not exist after the run — the skill never writes napkin's artifact.

assertions.name: nav_derived_from_tasks
assertions.description: Every nav row's serves: clause names a recurring task from the prompt's inventory (no orphan nav items), and every label in the first-shot walkthrough's Sees column exists verbatim in the produced nav map or surface inventory.

evals.name: review-mode-planted-leaks
evals.prompt: Audit our app's UI structure. Navigation config (nav.ts): top-level items = Dashboard, PartyAccounts, ProspectRecords, ClientRecords, DispatchAssignments, WorkOrders, RemittanceDocuments, ApprovalRequests, PendingReviews, CompliancePortal. Screen notes: RemittanceDocumentDetail renders columns remittance_id, party_account_id, agreement_id, amount, status. CompliancePortal is visible to every role from day one and is empty until a first audit cycle is configured. Empty states we already wrote: WorkOrders — "No jobs yet. Accept a quote to schedule your first job."; RemittanceDocuments — "Nothing to invoice. Completed jobs appear here ready to bill."; PendingReviews — "All clear — approvals you need to act on will land here." Who uses it: dispatchers assign and rebalance jobs all day and look up customers when they call; technicians work their day's job list on a phone; the office manager invoices, chases overdue payments, and approves timesheets and quotes. Audit this structure.
evals.expected_output: Review-mode contract: per-element findings citing literal nav entries/columns, principle rollup failing P1–P5 (10 schema-named nav items; Prospect/Client split; approval queues as nav destinations; raw foreign-key columns; day-one-for-everyone compliance module) while P6 passes (the empty-state copy genuinely teaches next actions), ordered fixes using canonical move names, first-shot walkthrough, no files touched.

assertions.name: planted_violations_not_passed
assertions.description: None of the five planted principles is marked PASS (FAIL or AT-RISK both acceptable).

assertions.name: control_principle_passes
assertions.description: The deliberately-good empty states pass — defeats flag-everything auditing.

assertions.name: canonical_fix_moves_used
assertions.description: Fixes use the canonical hyphenated move names verbatim.

assertions.name: findings_cite_fixture_elements
assertions.description: Each failed principle's finding cites the specific fixture element by name (e.g. ProspectRecords/ClientRecords nav entries, party_account_id or agreement_id column, CompliancePortal, ApprovalRequests or PendingReviews), not generic descriptions.
